The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following statements are true? 

I. $f(x)$ is defined at $x=2$

II. ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)$ exists

III. $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=2$
question.worked_solution:
By inspecting the graph, we can conclude the following:

- Statement I is true. Indeed, $f(2)=1.$

- Statement II is false. Indeed, from the graph we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}f(x) & =1, \\ {lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{+}}f(x) & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,  ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)$ doesn't exist

- Statement III is false.  The graph of the function breaks at $x=2$
and it's impossible to draw the graph without taking our pencil off of the paper.
